note: Content-quality scorecards from a Build OS deep audit: every repo read for the quality of its docs, evals, tests and CI, every grade backed by a quoted file and line, then an interview and a fix pass. Supersedes the earlier evidence-only scoring, which counted artifacts existing rather than holding up.

projects.title: FounderFirst
projects.notes: Its LLM-judge panel is now measurable, and is still unvalidated, which the docs now say. Everything the repo claimed about the panel was about how it is built, family-aware and fail-closed and injection-safe, and none of that is evidence it agrees with a human. There are now 40 human-labeled cases, class balanced 10 to 10 on each of the two binary gates, a metrics module reporting agreement next to the base rate it has to beat plus kappa and both per-class rates, and a runner that calls the shipped judge with the criteria copied from the live eval library. ENFORCED is empty on purpose: without a keyed run the runner prints SKIP rather than pass, and a pair that is absent is unmeasured rather than exempt. The arithmetic is PR-gated through pnpm build. FounderFirst now encrypts Plaid access tokens at rest, and closing that found three read paths that would have broken had the write been encrypted alone. It is the deepest system of the five and the only one with real resilience in the model path: bounded exponential backoff, hard timeouts, and a cheaper-model fallback where a spend cap is a fallback rather than a failure. Money is integer minor units by invariant, ingest dedupes exactly once on a shared external key, and three bespoke CI guards fail the build on any query that touches a tenant table without a tenant predicate. The autonomy ramp now states plainly that autonomy is off and documents how its thresholds get derived from production data. Pillar math: Product Judgment = avg(D1 good, D2 good, D7 good, R1 good, S6 good, S4 good, GEN3 good) = 7.0; System Design = avg(S1 good, S2 great, S3 good, S5 great, S8 good, GEN2 good) = 8.0; Evaluation = avg(E1 good, E2 good, E3 good, E5 good) = 7.0; Reliability & Ownership = avg(B1 great, B2 great, B3 good, B4 great, B5 good, SH3 good, SH8 good, SH10 great, GEN2 good) = 8.33; Safety = avg(E3 good, SH1 great, SH2 good, SH9 great, SH10 great) = 8.8; Economics = avg(S1 good, GEN3 good) = 7.0; Communication = avg(D1 good, SH4 good, D5 great, SH5 good) = 7.75; UX/UI & Interaction = avg(S4 good) = 7.0; Collaboration & Stakeholders = avg(D5 great, SH5 good, CS1 great) = 9.0. Overall = round(mean of 9 non-null pillars (7.681) x 10) = 77. Collaboration & Stakeholders is null: no stakeholder question was graded this run, so it stays a visible gap rather than a guess. Cost work 2026-08-02: docs/COST.md and scripts/cost-model.mjs give $2.00 per month per 4,000 transactions, $0.0005 all in. The headline is that 80% of transactions never reach a model at all, so the deterministic rule is worth more than the model cascade. Found and fixed the same 3x Opus price error Rally had, feeding ai_decisions. S1 stays GOOD: great needs a tested cheaper model. The 80% figure is a reading of a code comment, not a measurement, and the model is severely sensitive to it.
projects.next_focus: Next for FounderFirst: run pnpm eval:judge with a model credential. The harness, the labels and the floor are in place, so one keyed run turns the judge panel from unvalidated into measured and moves E2 from good to great. The kappa and both per-class rates belong in docs/EVALS.md section 8.5 in the same commit as the run.

projects.title: RoleOS
projects.notes: Its tool loop is bounded by three limits rather than one, and closing that gap surfaced a live defect: at the turn cap the loop returned the text of a tool_use response, which is the model asking for another tool, so a cut-short run handed back an empty string and no explanation. The notice is now folded into the answer text. A token and USD run budget joins the turn cap, distinct from the rolling-24h alert in lib/cost-budget.ts, which never throws and so cannot stop the run in front of it. No default budget ships until agent_runs holds real loop costs. RoleOS now gives candidates a privacy notice, per-table retention enforced by a nightly purge, and a working delete path across 18 tables, with what deletion does not cover stated plainly. It added retry across its single model call path and found a real money bug doing it: spend from earlier tool-loop turns was discarded when a later turn failed, so the daily budget guard never saw it. It holds the strongest structural safety guarantee in the portfolio: no send tool exists, the single outbound route returns 501, and a CI import ban enforces it, so no prompt and no refactor can make the agent send on a user's behalf. Production deploys are now gated on a green CI run, and a new injection test exercising real shipped code runs on every pull request. The retrieval SLA (precision@10 at or above 0.5, MRR at or above 0.7) is measured over 689 real postings and blocks a merge. Pillar math: Product Judgment = avg(D1 good, D2 good, D3 good, D7 good, R1 weak, S6 good, S4 good) = 6.57; System Design = avg(S1 good, S2 great, S3 good, S5 good, AG1 good, AG2 great, AG4 great, GEN2 good) = 8.12; Evaluation = avg(E1 good, E2 weak, E3 good, E4 good, E5 good) = 6.4; Reliability & Ownership = avg(B1 great, B2 great, B3 good, B4 weak, B5 good, SH3 good, SH8 good, SH10 great, GEN1 good, GEN2 good) = 7.6; Safety = avg(E3 good, SH1 great, SH2 great, SH9 good, SH10 great, AG4 great) = 9.0; Economics = avg(S1 good, AG2 great) = 8.5; Communication = avg(D1 good, SH4 good, D5 great, SH5 good) = 7.75; UX/UI & Interaction = avg(S4 good, SH6 good, GEN1 good) = 7.0; Collaboration & Stakeholders = avg(D5 great, SH5 good, CS1 great) = 9.0. Overall = round(mean of 9 non-null pillars (7.563) x 10) = 76. Collaboration & Stakeholders is null: no stakeholder question was graded this run, so it stays a visible gap rather than a guess. Cost work 2026-08-02: docs/COST.md and scripts/cost-model.mjs read agent/registry.json, giving $0.80 per candidate and $161/month at 200. The finding inverts the usual assumption: draft and code on Sonnet are 65% of spend and the Opus jobs a third, so output ceilings matter more than model tier. Prices were audited and RoleOS's were already correct. S1 stays GOOD: great needs a tested cheaper model, and there is no caching (documented, with the prompt sizes that would have to change first).
projects.next_focus: Next for RoleOS: run evals/retrieval/live/capture.ts and commit dataset.semantic.json. The eval now states plainly what it does and does not catch, and the runner will score and gate the semantic set the moment that file lands, but the retriever that actually ships is still unmeasured.

projects.title: Pulse
projects.notes: Pulse now retries a rate-limited model call with jitter inside a budget sized to the platform ceiling, then degrades to facts only, with 816 unit tests covering the ladder. It also has the clearest cost story of the five: caching takes 6,240 model calls a day down to 325, the before and after is labelled as modelled rather than metered, and a live spend counter now ships. Untrusted material is fenced as data at the prompt boundary and re-checked by a deterministic guard on every publish, and the guard fixture floors run offline in CI on every pull request. Pillar math: Product Judgment = avg(D1 great, D2 good, D7 good, R1 weak, S4 good, GEN3 great) = 7.5; System Design = avg(S1 great, S2 good, S3 weak, S5 good, S8 good) = 7.0; Evaluation = avg(E1 good, E2 good, E3 good, E4 good, E5 great) = 7.6; Reliability & Ownership = avg(B1 great, B2 great, B3 good, B4 good, B5 good, SH3 good, SH8 good, SH10 great) = 8.12; Safety = avg(E3 good, SH1 great, SH9 good, SH10 great) = 8.5; Economics = avg(S1 great, GEN3 great) = 10.0; Communication = avg(D1 great, SH4 good, D5 great, SH5 good) = 8.5; UX/UI & Interaction = avg(S4 good) = 7.0; Collaboration & Stakeholders = avg(D5 great, SH5 good, CS1 great) = 9.0. Overall = round(mean of 9 non-null pillars (8.069) x 10) = 81. Collaboration & Stakeholders is null: no stakeholder question was graded this run, so it stays a visible gap rather than a guess. E2 moves weak to good on 2026-08-02: judgeGroundedness now has a validation harness (evals/judge-metrics.ts, a 24-case set class balanced 12/12, Cohen's kappa reported beside the base rate and both per-class rates, grading the shipped judge). It stops at good, not great, because no keyed run has happened yet, so no kappa exists and ENFORCED ships empty. Structure alone caps at good. Found while doing it: npm run eval:groundedness had been crashing on ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND before scoring a single case, and no CI job ran any eval script, so it failed silently on every invocation. Both fixed; the check job now runs all three offline evals.
projects.next_focus: Next for Pulse: schedule the retention sweep and wire an alerting channel. The windows and the health thresholds are both defined and enforced in code, but nothing runs the sweep on a timer and nothing notifies anyone when a threshold trips.

projects.title: Rally
projects.notes: Its detection score is now reported against the number it has to beat. Case-level agreement is 0.844 against a 0.531 majority baseline, Cohen's kappa 0.684, and two null models are committed as functions rather than remembered figures: crediting every at-handle scores 0.703 agreement, which reads as respectable because half the set does credit somebody, and never proposing anything scores a perfect zero false-positive rate and 1.0 precision while carrying no signal at all. A false-positive rate quoted alone would have ranked that second one above the shipped detector. Rally has no LLM judge on this path: grading is exact set matching on helper and kind, so there is nothing to drift and nothing to validate, which is the stronger option rather than the cheaper one. Rally closed a recognition farming path found by its own design review: writing your own thanks now pays the author nothing, and a per-pair rolling allowance bounds what two people can mint, while the thank-you still posts publicly so genuine recognition is untouched. It also recovers a transient rate limit instead of silently dropping to its deterministic baseline, with per-call-site budgets and the provider SDK own-retries switched off so the two layers cannot multiply. It runs the most complete eval loop of the five: a 50-case labelled set with precision, recall and F1 floors that block a merge, alongside 45 adversarial Firestore rules tests where each test name states a promise the product makes. The recognition ledger awards exactly once under retry, proven by integration tests on deterministic event ids. Pillar math: Product Judgment = avg(D1 good, D2 good, D7 good, R1 weak, S4 good) = 6.4; System Design = avg(S1 good, S2 great, S3 weak, S5 good, S8 good) = 7.0; Evaluation = avg(E1 good, E2 great, E3 good, E5 good) = 7.75; Reliability & Ownership = avg(B1 great, B2 great, B3 good, B4 great, B5 good, SH3 good, SH10 great, GEN1 great, SH8 good) = 8.67; Safety = avg(E3 good, SH1 good, SH2 good, SH10 great, SH9 good) = 7.6; Economics = avg(S1 good) = 7.0; Communication = avg(D1 good, SH4 good, D5 great, SH5 good) = 7.75; UX/UI & Interaction = avg(S4 good, GEN1 great) = 8.5; Collaboration & Stakeholders = avg(D5 great, SH5 good, CS1 great) = 9.0. Overall = round(mean of 9 non-null pillars (7.574) x 10) = 76. Collaboration & Stakeholders is null: no stakeholder question was graded this run, so it stays a visible gap rather than a guess. Cost work 2026-08-02: docs/COST.md and scripts/cost-model.mjs now give a figure at volume ($5.40/month at 30 members) and detection is cached. Found and fixed a 3x error: MODEL_PRICING carried Opus at $15/$75, which is Opus-3-era pricing, and it fed the live meter via estimateCostUsd. S1 stays GOOD, not great: great needs a smaller model tested on Rally's own examples and no such run exists. The cascade routes bulk work to Haiku because Haiku is cheap, not because it was measured as good enough.
projects.next_focus: Next for Rally: publish one eval run with a live API key so the model layer is measured against the deterministic baseline rather than compared to itself, and schedule the retention sweep, which is written and enforced but not yet run by anything. The detection labels are one author's, so a second labeller would turn the kappa into genuine inter-rater agreement.

projects.title: Conduit
projects.notes: It now has a breaking-change policy and something that enforces it. docs/VERSIONING.md lists what counts as breaking rather than gesturing at a principle, sets a six-month window from the day a v2 becomes default with Deprecation and Sunset headers at T-0, direct notice at T+90 to tenants with recent traffic, and 410 Gone rather than 404 at T+180. None of that has run, because there is no v2 and no traffic, and the document says so. scripts/check-api-surface.mjs holds a committed snapshot of every route and response field with optionality recorded, since optional to required is a narrowing that would otherwise look like no change, and it runs on every pull request. Its tests are the ones that prove it fails: a removal, a rename, a narrowing, and a guard that the snapshot is non-empty, because a regex parser matching nothing would report unchanged forever. What it cannot catch, a field keeping its name and changing meaning, is stated in the script rather than implied away. Its agent loop is bounded by three limits rather than one: a step cap, a token and USD run budget, and repeated-state detection, each naming itself and returning a partial trace with an explanation. Loop detection keys on the tool call together with its result, so a poller does not false-halt, and it runs on successful calls only, because a repeated error is the information the model needs to recover. A follow-up caught the notice stopping at the library boundary, where an API caller would have seen a partial answer indistinguishable from a complete one, and carried it out to the wire contract. No default budget ships: choosing one needs real run costs and there is no traffic yet. Conduit now evaluates what it ships, and an architecture review caught the repo overclaiming: the guardrail engine is not wired to any request path, so the docs that called it an enforced floor were corrected in place and the injection grade dropped to weak. The judge is measured rather than assumed. On a 30-case class-balanced set, groundedness judging reaches Cohen's kappa 0.93 and is the one pair the repo claims; relevance judging sits at 0.13 and is explicitly barred from gating output until tuned. The cheap judge model turned out to reject every answer, which a raw catch rate would have shown as flawless. Guardrails catch every attack in the golden set (recall 1.00) while refusing 4 of 16 safe inputs (precision 0.83), and a default-deny agent loop means a side-effecting tool cannot run without explicit authority. Pillar math: Product Judgment = avg(D1 good, D2 good, D3 good, D6 good, D7 good, S4 good, S6 good, R1 good, API1 good) = 7.0; System Design = avg(S1 good, S2 great, S3 great, S5 good, S8 good, AG1 good, AG2 great, AG4 great, API1 good, API3 great) = 8.5; Evaluation = avg(E1 good, E2 good, E3 great, E4 good, E5 good) = 7.6; Reliability & Ownership = avg(D4 good, B1 good, B2 great, B3 good, B5 good, SH3 good, SH8 good, SH10 good) = 7.38; Safety = avg(E3 great, SH1 great, SH2 great, SH7 great, SH9 good, SH10 good, AG4 great) = 9.14; Economics = avg(S1 good, AG2 great) = 8.5; Communication = avg(D1 good, SH4 weak, API2 good, API3 great, D5 great, SH5 good) = 7.5; UX/UI & Interaction = avg(S4 good) = 7.0; Collaboration & Stakeholders = avg(D5 great, SH5 good, CS1 great) = 9.0. Overall = round(mean of 9 non-null pillars (7.58) x 10) = 76. Collaboration & Stakeholders is null: no stakeholder question was graded this run, so it stays a visible gap rather than a guess. Cost work 2026-08-02: docs/COST.md and scripts/cost-model.mjs parse the routing table and prices from core.ts, giving $66.30 per tenant per month and showing volume is a bad proxy for spend (chat is 78% of calls and 36% of cost). Also fixed: computeCostUsd returned 0 for any model missing from the price table, so a genuinely free model and an unpriced one produced the same number. S1 stays GOOD: great needs a tested cheaper model, and the gateway cache is deliberately off under D11 for tenant isolation.
projects.next_focus: Next for Conduit: record the 90 second walkthrough. SH4 is now the only weak question left and the README still carries an empty demo placeholder at line 14. The console is public at nikjain15.github.io/conduit against a mock gateway, so a silent GIF needs no login and is the cheapest remaining point on the board.
